# fastf 3.12.0: a move can never half-delete a project

Nothing about an existing project changes. Every `PROJECT_INFO.md`,
`config.toml` and template works untouched, and no command, flag or file format
was removed.

This release comes out of a real incident. A cross-drive move from an sshfs
mount deleted 1460 of a project's 1473 files and then stopped, and `fastf
reconcile` kept saying the source was untouched. Nothing was lost, because the
copy had already been verified. But a move must never depend on luck about
which side fails, so this release changes how a move ends.

## The original leaves the library in one step

After the copy is verified, the original is no longer deleted where it stands.
Deleting a folder takes many steps, and anything that stops it part of the way
(a read-only folder inside, a file another program holds open, a network drop)
used to leave part of the project behind, still listed as the project.

Now the original is renamed, in one step, to a hidden folder beside it, and
only then removed.

- If the rename cannot happen, for example because a program on Windows has a
  file in it open, the move says **the original is still there, whole, and
  nothing in it was removed**, and why. The moved copy is complete. Once the
  reason is gone, `fastf reconcile` finishes the move without copying again,
  and until then the app lists both copies.
- If the removal stops part of the way, what is left is a hidden folder that is
  never listed as a project. `fastf reconcile` removes it.
- Nothing is removed that exists nowhere else. Before the original is set
  aside, and again before its hidden copy is removed, fastf checks that
  everything in it is what the move recorded and is still in the moved copy.

`fastf delete` works the same way: the project leaves the library in one
rename, and a removal that stops part of the way never leaves half of it listed.

## Links travel as links

Symbolic links, and junctions on Windows, used to stop a cross-drive move or
copy. They are now carried as links, pointing exactly where they pointed.
Nothing behind a link is copied, and removing the original never deletes
through one. A link whose target is missing, as `node_modules/.bin` often
holds, moves like any other. When a link may mean something different at the
new place (a relative one that climbs out of the project, an absolute one into
the original folder), the move names it.

On Windows a symbolic link can only be made with Developer Mode on; junctions
need nothing. A move that would need one says so before copying anything.

## Before a byte is copied

A cross-drive move now finds out at the start what used to stop it at the end,
and names every problem at once:

- entries it cannot copy: a socket, a pipe, a device, an entry the filesystem
  lists but will not let it examine, another filesystem mounted inside;
- whether it can write in the source base, since a move has to remove the
  original afterwards. A read-only base, or a share you can only read, is
  refused;
- whether the target has room;
- whether the target can hold every name. Two names that differ only in case on
  a drive that ignores case, a character the drive forbids, or a name too long
  are all found in seconds.

## Network mounts

- An sshfs mount with `follow_symlinks` shows a link as whatever it points to,
  so fastf could neither see a project's links nor remove the original without
  deleting through them. That was the incident's mount. A move from such a
  mount, and a delete on one, are now refused, and the message names the
  option.
- sshfs by default refuses to read any link that climbs with `..`, which is
  every link in `node_modules/.bin`. The move names `-o no_contain_symlinks`.

To move projects over sshfs, mount without `follow_symlinks` and with
`-o no_contain_symlinks`.

## Reconcile says what is on disk

Every line `fastf reconcile` prints now names the project, its move record, and
what is actually on disk, never "left untouched" about a folder it had not
looked at. A move that fastf 3.11 or older left half-deleted is finished when
what is left is provably a duplicate, and otherwise every difference is listed.
A move another machine began is reported, not acted on.

An unfinished move written by 3.12 is reported, not acted on, by 3.11 and
older. If you run two versions against shared drives, finish moves with 3.12.

## Fixes

- A folder rename waits longer for Windows' indexer or a virus scanner to let
  go of a freshly copied tree. Before, a verified copy could be thrown away at
  the last step.
- A warning too long for the status line, or an error with several lines, now
  opens in a dialog instead of showing its first few words.
